answers.answer:
Short answer: the SCOPe classification hasn't changed, but how much each assignment can be trusted has. In SCOPe 2.08 (the current release; periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16), all three structures sit in the same place: class a (all-alpha) > fold a.47 'STAT-like' > superfamily a.47.2 't-snare proteins' > family a.47.2.1 't-snare proteins'. So fragment-based placement was never 'corrected' to a different fold or superfamily. What changed is the evidence attached to each entry and how each was assigned.

1) 1br0 and 1ez3 (d1br0a_, sunid 17772; d1ez3a_, d1ez3b_, d1ez3c_, sunids 17768-17770). These are manually curated domains under protein 'Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain' (sunid 47663), Rattus norvegicus (sunid 47664). They carry the comment 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat'. In 2.08 each also carries the inconsistency flag 'ms': it is missing some secondary structures that made up less than one-third of the common domain. In SCOP 1.75, d1br0a_ had the same fragment comment plus 'mutant', but no formal inconsistency flag. SCOPe now formally marks these entries as incomplete versions of the domain.

2) 1dn1 chain B (the full domain, from the nSec1/Munc18-syntaxin 1A complex). It was curated in SCOP 1.75 as d1dn1b_ (sunid 17771) beside d1dn1a_ in e.25.1.1 (Sec1/Munc18). PDB made 1dn1 obsolete on 2008-03-25, replacing it with 3c98. The entry had no domains in SCOPe 2.01. By 2.06 it was back under a new sunid, 302344, now placed under 'automated matches' (sunid 191190, species node 311131) with the comment 'automated match to d3c98b_'. 2.07 and 2.08 keep it the same way. The curated full-length reference is now d3c98b_ (sunid 173092), which is in the syntaxin 1A / rat node with no inconsistency flags. d1dn1b_ is no longer an independently curated assignment. It inherits a.47.2.1 by matching the superseding structure. Use 3c98 rather than 1dn1 as the coordinate template or representative.

What this means biologically:
- The fragments' family/superfamily placement is supported by homology. Sequence identity to syntaxin 1A and to the complete Habc domain in d3c98b_ links them to the t-SNARE family/superfamily: Sso1, Vam3p N-terminal domain, Syntaxin 6, Vti1-like. Their fold label is not independent structural evidence, though. The a.47 fold is defined as '4 long helices; bundle, left-handed twist (coiled coil); right-handed superhelix'. A three-helix fragment flagged 'ms' does not have the complete fold on its own. Its resemblance to a single spectrin repeat (a.7) shows that three-helix bundles look alike by convergence. Fold assignment for these entries is inherited from the full-domain homologs, not something the fragments show themselves.
- Similarity at the fold level, here a.47 shared with the STAT superfamily a.47.1, does not imply homology or shared function. Shared ancestry is claimed only within superfamily a.47.2, and specific function only at the family/protein level.
- Unsafe transfers:
  - Don't use the fragment structures as full-domain templates.
  - Don't infer Munc18 binding or the 'closed' syntaxin conformation from 1br0 or 1ez3. Those features need the full complex, as in 1dn1 or 3c98, together with chain A (e.25.1.1).
  - Don't count the automated d1dn1b_ as independent curated evidence alongside d3c98b_.
  - Don't pick an 'ms'-flagged fragment as a representative when a complete domain exists.
- External evidence still needed for any functional claim: PDB obsolescence and supersession records, sequence alignment or UniProt mapping to syntaxin-1A residue ranges, the primary literature on these structures, and binding or mutagenesis data.
